nonLabourLines.description: Third-party tooling (CI, observability, email service) - indicative

assumptions: The rate card provided is a PLACEHOLDER: all project members are currently a single undifferentiated 'Team member' role at $75/hr with only 1 FTE available. Costs are indicative only until real roles (e.g. backend, frontend, QA, PM) and their respective hourly rates are assigned.

With only 1 FTE available, the 190 story points in this backlog (24 tasks) represent a large amount of work relative to capacity. At a rough planning ratio of ~6-8 hours per point (accounting for design, build, test, review) this backlog is roughly 1,140-1,520 hours of effort; we've used 1,200 hours as a central planning estimate. This is likely to take a single FTE close to 30 weeks (~7 months) of full-time work, so either timeline expectations should be adjusted or headcount increased.

No historical actuals (real spend/velocity data) exist for this project yet, so the effort-to-hours conversion (points -> hours) is based on generic industry heuristics, not this team's demonstrated velocity. Treat the estimate as low-confidence until a few sprints of real data are available.

Non-labour costs are indicative placeholders for CI/CD tooling, observability/error-dashboard tooling, and transactional email service subscriptions; Stripe's own transaction fees are usage-based and not included as a fixed project cost.
Priority breakdown is derived by allocating the 1,200 planned hours in proportion to each task's story points, then costing at $75/hr, then grouping by the task's declared priority.

P80 and P90 scenarios add 20% and 35% contingency respectively over the P50 baseline to account for the single-FTE bottleneck, the complexity of PW-8 (legacy Oracle migration of 400k customers/2M invoice lines) and PW-7 (Stripe payments/webhooks/reconciliation), both of which carry higher technical and data-integrity risk.

Estimate assumes the single Team member is capable of covering all disciplines (backend, frontend, data migration, QA) required by the backlog; in reality this backlog needs multiple specialized roles, which should be reflected in a future, non-placeholder rate card.
input.reasoning: Since the rate card only defines one generic 'Team member' role at $75/hr with 1 FTE, all labour was costed under that single line. Total effort was estimated by converting the 190 total story points across 24 backlog items into hours using a standard planning heuristic (~6.3 hrs/point on average), yielding 1,200 hours ($90,000) as the central (P50) labour estimate. A modest $3,000 non-labour allowance was added for supporting tooling (CI/CD, observability, transactional email), giving a P50 total of $93,000. P80 and P90 scenarios layer on 20% and 35% contingency respectively to reflect the significant delivery risk: only 1 FTE is available against a backlog that logically requires multiple specialized roles (backend/API, frontend, data engineering, QA), and two of the highest-risk items (Stripe payment integration PW-7, and legacy Oracle data migration PW-8) carry meaningful technical/integration risk that could blow past a naive estimate. Priority-based cost breakdown was computed by allocating hours proportionally to story points within each priority band and costing at the flat rate. Because there are no historical actuals for this team/project, all effort figures should be treated as provisional until real velocity data and a proper multi-role rate card are available.

reductions.description: Descope or defer the three Low-priority, non-critical-path items (PW-12 Support ticket submission, PW-19 Usage analytics/reporting, PW-23 Contract tests against helpdesk API) to a later phase.
reductions.effect: Removes roughly 18 story points (~151 hours) of Low-priority scope from the initial delivery; can be revisited in a follow-on phase once core portal functions are live.

reductions.description: Defer PW-18 (Admin back-office for support staff) and PW-24 (Decommission legacy portal) until after go-live, since support staff can use existing tools and the legacy system can run in parallel briefly.
reductions.effect: Removes 21 story points (~132 hours) from the initial build; legacy system stays live a little longer and support agents temporarily keep using current tools.

reductions.description: Simplify PW-14 (Multi-currency support) to launch with a single settlement currency (USD) and display-only FX conversion for EUR/PLN, deferring full multi-currency settlement.
reductions.effect: Cuts roughly 60% of the estimated effort for this feature (about 8 points / 60 hours), reducing integration complexity with FX providers and settlement logic at launch.

reductions.description: Reduce non-labour tooling spend by starting with free/open-source tiers for CI and observability tooling (e.g. GitHub Actions free tier, open-source tracing) instead of paid subscriptions during the initial build phase.
reductions.effect: Halves the indicative $3,000 non-labour tooling allowance for the initial phase; paid tiers can be adopted later as usage grows.

reductions.description: Increase headcount from 1 FTE to 2-3 appropriately-skilled FTEs (once real roles/rates are defined) rather than stretching a single generalist across the full backlog.
reductions.effect: This is a schedule-risk mitigation rather than a direct cost saving: it does not reduce total labour cost but substantially de-risks the ~30-week single-FTE timeline and the associated risk of overruns on high-complexity items like PW-7 and PW-8, which is where most contingency cost (the P80/P90 uplift) currently sits.
